title: SA-1 Guild
summary: The first Soviet SAM: 56 fixed sites in two rings around Moscow, command-guided.

title: SA-2 Guideline
summary: The classic six-launcher site around a Fan Song radar: radio-command-guided, and the SAM US crews met over North Vietnam.

title: SA-3 Goa
summary: Command-guided by the Low Blow radar from two- or four-missile launchers; the system that downed an F-117.

title: SA-4 Ganef
summary: A tracked, ramjet-powered army SAM carrying two missiles per launcher.

title: SA-5 Gammon
summary: A very long-range strategic SAM guided by the Square Pair continuous-wave radar.

title: SA-6 Gainful
summary: A mobile tracked battery: one Straight Flush radar, four three-missile launchers, semi-active homing.

title: SA-7 Grail
summary: A shoulder-fired, rear-aspect infrared missile: nothing on the RWR, and flares proved highly effective against it.

title: SA-8 Gecko
summary: An amphibious six-wheeled vehicle carrying its own Land Roll radar and missiles: a self-contained short-range SAM.

title: SA-9 Gaskin
summary: Four infrared missiles on a BRDM-2 scout car with a passive detector: nothing for a radar warning receiver to see, short range.

title: SA-10 Grumble
summary: A long-range, vertically launched SAM: Flap Lid fire control, Clam Shell low-altitude and Big Bird search radars.

title: SA-11 Gadfly
summary: The SA-6's successor: each tracked launcher carries its own Fire Dome radar and four semi-active homing missiles.

title: SA-12 Gladiator / Giant
summary: The army's tracked long-range system, with separate missiles against aircraft (Gladiator) and ballistic missiles (Giant).

title: SA-13 Gopher
summary: Four infrared missiles on a tracked MT-LB with a range-only radar: a short-range, low-altitude SAM meant mainly for helicopters.

title: SA-14 Gremlin
summary: A shoulder-fired missile with a cooled infrared seeker: harder to decoy than the SA-7, with limited head-on capability.

title: SA-15 Gauntlet
summary: A tracked, self-contained vehicle with its own Scrum Half radars and eight vertically launched command-guided missiles.

title: SA-16 Gimlet
summary: The simplified first Igla: a shoulder-fired infrared missile with optional IFF, credited with Gulf War and Kosovo hits.

title: SA-17 Grizzly
summary: The Buk with the 9M317 missile: a larger envelope against aircraft and the ability to engage ballistic missiles.

title: SA-18 Grouse
summary: The full Igla: a shoulder-fired missile whose infrared and ultraviolet seeker resists flares, with head-on capability.

title: SA-19 Grison
summary: Twin 30 mm cannon and eight command-guided missiles on one tracked vehicle with its own Hot Shot radar.

title: A-10 Thunderbolt II
summary: The Warthog: a straight-wing, armoured close air support jet built around the 30 mm GAU-8 cannon.

title: AH-64D Apache Longbow
summary: The US Army's twin-engine attack helicopter, flown from Panama and Desert Storm to Afghanistan; the Longbow adds a mast-mounted radar.

title: AJS 37 Viggen
summary: A Swedish canard-delta attack aircraft built to fly from road bases, with a thrust reverser and anti-ship missiles.

title: AV-8B Harrier II
summary: A vectored-thrust jump jet: vertical or short take-off, flown by the US Marines for close air support.

title: Bf 109 K-4
summary: The final production version of the most-produced fighter in history, Germany's standard fighter throughout the war.

title: C-101 Aviojet
summary: Spain's two-seat jet trainer with an internal weapons bay.

title: C-130J Super Hercules
summary: The modernised four-turboprop tactical transport: new engines, glass cockpit, three crew.

title: CH-47F Chinook
summary: The tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter that has carried troops, guns and supplies for every war since Vietnam.

title: Christen Eagle II
summary: A two-seat kit-built aerobatic biplane, flown by the Eagles Aerobatic Team.

title: F4U-1D Corsair
summary: The bent-wing Navy and Marine fighter of the Pacific war, with a kill ratio better than 11 to 1.

title: F-4 Phantom II
summary: The big two-seat Cold War fighter-bomber; the F-4E added an internal gun and slats after Vietnam.

title: F-5 Tiger II
summary: A small, cheap supersonic fighter for US allies, and a long-serving adversary aircraft that stands in for the MiG-21.

title: F-14 Tomcat
summary: The Navy's swing-wing fleet defence fighter: two crew, AWG-9 radar and AIM-54 Phoenix.

title: F-15C Eagle
summary: A twin-engine air superiority fighter with more than 104 air-to-air victories and no losses.

title: F-15E Strike Eagle
summary: The two-seat, long-range, all-weather strike derivative of the Eagle.

title: F-16 Fighting Falcon
summary: A single-engine multirole fighter: fly-by-wire, 9 g, and the US Air Force's main strike and SEAD aircraft.

title: F-86 Sabre
summary: The swept-wing day fighter that met the MiG-15 over Korea.

title: F-100 Super Sabre
summary: The first US Air Force fighter supersonic in level flight; a fighter-bomber and fast FAC in Vietnam.

title: F/A-18 Hornet
summary: A carrier-capable fighter and attack aircraft that one pilot can switch between roles on the same sortie.

title: Fw 190 A-8
summary: Kurt Tank's radial-engined fighter, armoured and up-gunned in the A-8 to attack American heavy bombers.

title: Fw 190 D-9
summary: The long-nosed, Jumo-powered Fw 190 that entered service in late 1944.

title: I-16
summary: The first front-line monoplane fighter with retractable gear, flown in Spain, China, Mongolia and in 1941.

title: J-11A
summary: China's licence-assembled Su-27SK, with new displays and the R-77 missile.

title: JF-17 Thunder
summary: A lightweight Pakistani–Chinese multirole fighter powered by the RD-93.

title: Ka-50 Black Shark
summary: A single-seat Russian attack helicopter with coaxial rotors and the first helicopter ejection seat in service.

title: L-39 Albatros
summary: The Warsaw Pact's standard jet trainer, with armed light-attack versions.

title: La-7
summary: The refined Soviet radial-engined fighter of 1944–45, flown by the top Soviet ace Ivan Kozhedub.

title: MB-339
summary: Italy's two-seat jet trainer and light attack aircraft, flown by the Frecce Tricolori.

title: Mi-8MTV-2 Hip
summary: The armed transport version of the Mi-8, the most-produced helicopter in the world.

title: Mi-24P Hind-F
summary: The Soviet gunship that could also carry eight troops; the Mi-24P has a fixed twin-barrel 30 mm cannon.

title: MiG-15
summary: The Soviet swept-wing jet fighter that shocked UN air forces over Korea, armed with 37 mm and 23 mm cannon.

title: MiG-19
summary: The first Soviet fighter supersonic in level flight; the MiG-19P added radar for all-weather interception.

title: MiG-21
summary: The small delta-wing Mach 2 fighter: the most-produced supersonic jet in history.

title: MiG-29 Fulcrum
summary: A twin-engine Soviet fighter with a helmet sight and R-73 missiles, built to counter the F-15 and F-16.

title: Mirage 2000C
summary: France's fly-by-wire delta interceptor, armed with Super 530D and Magic II missiles.

title: Mirage F1
summary: A swept-wing French fighter sold to eleven countries and flown in many wars.

title: Mosquito FB Mk VI
designation: de Havilland Mosquito FB Mk VI
summary: The fast wooden twin-engined fighter-bomber that needed no defensive guns.

title: OH-58D Kiowa Warrior
summary: The US Army's armed scout helicopter, with its ball-shaped sight above the rotor, flown from the Persian Gulf to Afghanistan.

title: P-47D Thunderbolt
summary: The heaviest single-engined fighter of the war: eight .50 calibre guns, a turbosupercharged radial, and a fearsome fighter-bomber.

title: P-51D Mustang
summary: The long-range escort fighter that took US bombers to Berlin and back; Merlin-powered, with six .50 calibre guns.

title: SA 342 Gazelle
summary: The light Franco-British helicopter that introduced the fenestron tail fan; the SA 342M hunts tanks with HOT missiles.

title: Spitfire LF Mk IX
summary: The elliptical-winged British fighter; the Merlin 66-powered Mark IX answered the Fw 190.

title: Su-25 Frogfoot
summary: An armoured Soviet close air support jet; the Su-25T adds Vikhr anti-tank missiles.

title: Su-27 Flanker
summary: A large, long-range Soviet air superiority fighter with ten missile stations.

title: Su-33 Flanker-D
summary: The carrier-based Flanker: canards, folding wings and a ski-jump launch from Admiral Kuznetsov.

title: T-45 Goshawk
summary: The carrier-capable Hawk derivative in which Navy and Marine Corps strike pilots learn jets.

title: UH-1H Huey
summary: The utility helicopter that defined the Vietnam War and served every US armed service; more than 16,000 built.

title: Yak-52
summary: A Soviet aerobatic primary trainer, built in Romania, that has also hunted drones over Ukraine.

title: Mark 81 general-purpose bomb
summary: The smallest Mark 80 bomb: a 250 lb low-drag bomb remembered for Vietnam's 'snake and nape' close air support.

title: Mark 82 general-purpose bomb
summary: The 500 lb low-drag bomb that is one of the most common air-dropped weapons in the world, with conical, Snakeye or ballute tails.

title: Mark 83 general-purpose bomb
summary: The 1,000 lb member of the Mark 80 family, used most by the US Navy and as the warhead of the GBU-16 and GBU-32.

title: Mark 84 general-purpose bomb
summary: The 2,000 lb heavyweight of the Mark 80 series, dropped by the thousand in Desert Storm and the warhead of the GBU-10 and GBU-31.

title: FAB-250 high-explosive bomb
summary: The Soviet 250 kg high-explosive bomb, from the 1946 bomber model to the low-drag M-62 for fighter-bombers.

title: FAB-500 high-explosive bomb
summary: The Soviet and Russian 500 kg high-explosive bomb, in service in one form or another since 1931.

title: OFAB-250-270 fragmentation bomb
summary: A short, heavy Soviet high-explosive fragmentation bomb, with a case made to break into fragments.

title: CBU-87 Combined Effects Munition
summary: The US Air Force's 1,000 lb class cluster bomb of 202 combined-effects bomblets, introduced in 1986.

title: CBU-97 Sensor Fuzed Weapon
summary: A cluster bomb whose 40 Skeet projectiles search for vehicles with infrared and laser sensors and fire down through their roofs.

title: Mk 20 Rockeye II cluster bomb
summary: The Navy's anti-armour cluster bomb of 247 shaped-charge bomblets, dropped in the thousands by Marines in Desert Storm.

title: RBK-250 and RBK-500 cluster bombs
summary: Soviet and Russian disposable cluster bombs whose cases carry fragmentation, anti-tank, concrete-breaking or incendiary loads.

title: Mark 77 fire bomb
summary: The US successor to napalm: a canister of thickened fuel used by the Marine Corps in 1991 and 2003.

title: Mk 76 and BDU-33 practice bombs
summary: The 25 lb blue practice bombs that let Navy and Air Force crews practise bombing and see each hit by its smoke or flash.

title: Hydra 70 (2.75 in) rocket
summary: The 2.75 in rocket that began as the 'Mighty Mouse' bomber-killer and became the standard rocket of US attack helicopters.

title: Zuni 5 in rocket
summary: The Navy's 5 in rocket of 1957, fired from four-tube LAU-10 pods and credited with an A-4 Skyhawk's only MiG kill.

title: S-5 57 mm rocket
summary: The small Soviet rocket of 1955, derived from a German wartime design and fired from pods of up to 32.

title: S-8 80 mm rocket
summary: The Soviet 80 mm rocket of 1984, with anti-armour, runway-attack and fuel-air warheads, fired from B-8 pods.

title: S-13 122 mm rocket
summary: A Soviet 122 mm rocket built to penetrate runways, shelters and bunkers, fired from five-tube launchers.

title: S-24 240 mm rocket
summary: A heavy Soviet rocket with a 123 kg warhead, carried singly on pylons.

title: High Velocity Aircraft Rocket (HVAR)
summary: The 5 in 'Holy Moses' rocket of the Second World War and Korea, fired from Thunderbolts, Corsairs and Skyraiders.

title: AIM-9 Sidewinder
summary: The heat-seeking dogfight missile of the US Navy since 1956, copied by the Soviets and still in production as the AIM-9X.

title: AIM-7 Sparrow
summary: The West's main radar-guided missile from the late 1950s to the 1990s, which homes on radar energy the fighter reflects off its target.

title: AIM-120 AMRAAM
summary: The active-radar "fire and forget" missile that replaced the Sparrow, carried by US fighters of every service since 1991.

title: AIM-54 Phoenix
summary: The F-14 Tomcat's long-range fleet-defence missile: up to six fired at once, each guided to a different target.

title: K-13 (R-3) "Atoll"
summary: The Soviet Union's reverse-engineered Sidewinder, so close a copy that parts of the two missiles interchange.

title: R-60 "Aphid"
summary: A tiny 44 kg Soviet dogfight missile, among the lightest and most agile in the world when it appeared in the 1970s.

title: R-73 "Archer"
summary: The Soviet dogfight missile that a pilot could aim with a helmet sight at targets up to 40° off the nose.

title: R-27 "Alamo"
summary: The Flanker and Fulcrum's medium-range missile, built in radar, infrared and anti-radiation versions on one airframe.

title: R-77 "Adder"
summary: Russia's answer to the AMRAAM, an active-radar missile steered by distinctive lattice tail fins.

title: R-40 "Acrid"
summary: One of the largest air-to-air missiles ever built, made for the MiG-25 to catch Mach 3 bombers.

title: R.550 Magic
summary: France's dogfight missile, built to fit Sidewinder launchers and carried by every Mirage from the III to the 2000.

title: Super 530
summary: The French radar-guided missile of the Mirage F1 and Mirage 2000, built to snap up at high targets.

title: PL-5
summary: A Chinese infrared dogfight missile descended from the Sidewinder via the Soviet K-13, carried by the JF-17.

title: PL-12
summary: China's first active-radar beyond-visual-range missile, exported as the SD-10 and carried by the JF-17.

title: M61 Vulcan
summary: The six-barrel 20 mm Gatling gun that has armed US fighters of every service since 1959.

title: GAU-8 Avenger
summary: The A-10's seven-barrel 30 mm tank-killing gun, so heavy that the aircraft was built around it.

title: GAU-12 Equalizer
summary: The Marine Corps Harrier's five-barrel 25 mm gun, carried in a belly pod; the F-35's GAU-22 is its four-barrel cousin.

title: M39 cannon
summary: The US Air Force's 20 mm revolver cannon of the 1950s, proven in Korea and still in the F-5's nose.

title: DEFA 550 series
summary: France's 30 mm revolver cannon, the standard gun of every French gun-armed fighter from 1954 until the Rafale.

title: ADEN cannon
summary: The 30 mm revolver cannon of every British gun-armed jet from the Hunter in 1954 to the Tornado.

title: GSh-23
summary: A Soviet twin-barrel 23 mm cannon in which each barrel's firing works the other, carried by the MiG-21 and JF-17.

title: GSh-30-1
summary: A light single-barrel 30 mm gun in the wing root of the MiG-29 and every Flanker.

title: GSh-6-23
summary: A six-barrel 23 mm gun that powers itself with its own gas, with one of the highest rates of fire of any autocannon.

title: Brevity words
summary: The multi-service radio code words shared by the Army, Marine Corps, Navy and Air Force, with where NATO's meaning may differ.

title: Joint terms and abbreviations
summary: CAS, SEAD, JTAC and ROE, the missions from strike to counterair, the air defenses aircraft face, and the words each service uses differently.

title: Airfield and ATC terms
summary: Runway markings and signs, the traffic pattern, the military overhead pattern and the standard radio words, with ICAO's definitions where they differ.

title: Carrier terms
summary: Marshal, platform, the groove and the ball: the Navy's shipboard words, and where they differ from the brevity list.

title: Air combat terms
summary: The 3/9 line, the bubble, pursuit curves, corner airspeed and the yo-yos and scissors of basic fighter maneuvers.

title: Flight terms
summary: Lift, drag, load factor, corner speed, Mach number and the afterburner for the jet, and ETL, vortex ring state and autorotation for the rotor.

title: Navigation terms
summary: Radials, bearings, variation and deviation, station passage, waypoints, RAIM and the military grid.

title: Weapons terms
summary: Fuzes, low-drag and retarded bombs, rockets, guided missiles, laser-guided weapons, and the chaff and flares that decoy a threat.
